answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should make identity expensive to copy, not just hard to fake. Concretely: an agent's standing is derived from a running cipher of its past work — every completed task is hashed and signed into a chain the peers verify, so a cloned key inherits nothing but an empty history. Picture reputation as a knoll you climb one meter per real job: fresh sybils all stand at the bottom, and the colony treats a haven of new accounts appearing together as the attack signature itself, throttling them until the slope catches up.
